name: spatial-biofilm-growth
title: Spatial biofilm growth: a developed colony with a real substrate gradient
question:
Starting from a small inoculum of 40 agents, does the viva-biofilm spatial
engine grow a visibly developed 2D biofilm — hundreds of agents, a
measurable thickness above the substratum, and a genuine substrate-limitation
gradient (boundary richer than substratum) — within a short, deterministic,
non-swept run?

report.title: Spatial biofilm growth
report.evidence_quality: deterministic single run, fixed parameters (no sweep)
report.objective:
Demonstrate the viva-biofilm spatial engine's headline capability: a
developed 2D biofilm colony with realistic spatial structure, rendered as
interactive figures, anchored by the chemostat-equivalence well-mixed
validation.
report.result:
From 40 seed agents, 150 steps (dt=0.05 d) at a 32x48 grid grew the colony
to 640 agents with a biofilm thickness of 11.7 um. The solute field shows
a clear substrate-limitation gradient: substratum-third mean 0.438 g/m^3
vs boundary-third mean 0.894 g/m^3 (ratio 0.49) — the biofilm is
demonstrably drawing down substrate near the surface it consumes it at.
report.interpretation:
A small inoculum develops into a spatially structured, substrate-limited
biofilm using fixed, non-tuned parameters — the qualitative behavior
iDynoMiCS-2 is designed to reproduce, now visualized interactively and
reproducibly in seconds rather than minutes.
